target.necessary_condition: One ReplicateWALEntryRequest contains at least two WALEntry keys whose encodedRegionName values differ; the first key must also resolve to a serving region before the loop.

selectors_reviewed.workload: Creates a one-region table with two replicas and a separate table without replicas, then writes rows. WAL source batches may contain edits from both tables, but RegionReplicaReplicationEndpoint sends them through EntryBuffers before replay.
Creates a one-region table with three replicas, writes 100 rows, then explicitly passes a one-entry list to RegionReplicaSinkWriter.append.

shared_request_path.finding: replicate appends source entries to EntryBuffers; after IOException it retries the context and restarts writer threads without constructing a cross-region request.
EntryBuffers keys RegionEntryBuffer by encodedRegionName and serializes writes per region. RegionEntryBuffer also interns each entry key to its region's name.

The sink forwards one region buffer; each replica callable retains that entries list across RPC retries, skips changed-region locations, and calls buildReplicateWALEntryRequest with the target replica's non-null encoded region name.
The builder writes the same supplied encodedRegionName into every protobuf WALKey. This independently prevents a mixed-region replay request even if a source list were mixed.

other_replication_path: HBaseInterClusterReplicationEndpoint.replicateEntries uses ReplicationProtbufUtil.replicateWALEntry and the AdminService.replicateWALEntry RPC, not the selected RSRpcServices.replay method.
fault_model_assessment: An injected IOException can abort a read, send, or replay call and cause a retry, skip, or failure. It does not mutate WALKey fields or the protobuf builder. Both reviewed selectors therefore retain the same request-building invariant under exception-only injection; neither has a source-supported mechanism to make the selected mixed-region predicate true.
decision: No new numeric-thread diagnostic or fault campaign for these two selectors. This is a source/fault-model feasibility finding, not a claim that the guard is unreachable from every possible external or malformed RPC request.
